source.title: Scaling convolutional neural networks achieves expert level seizure detection in neonatal EEG
source.authors: Robert Hogan; S. Mathieson; Aurel Luca; S. Ventura; Sean Griffin; G. Boylan; John M. O'Toole

record.file_problem: None noted; full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling trends in a new modality and task: supervised neonatal EEG seizure detection with convolutional neural networks, rather than language-model pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The paper measures performance as training-data and model size vary, including approximate power-law trends, double-descent dips, and a distribution-dependent degradation. It does not test language-model cross-entropy or compute-optimal language-model allocations.
record.test_reason: The study trains five ConvNeXt CNNs (38.7k to 20.6M parameters) and sub-samples training data for neonatal EEG seizure classification. It reports how MCC, Pearson r and error rate change with data and model scale, and calls the gains approximate power laws. That is a new-modality result bearing on V5. It does not measure language-model loss, compute-optimal splits or fitted exponents, so V1–V4, V6 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that scaling data (up to 50% MCC gain) and model size (up to 15% MCC gain) improves neonatal seizure detection, with double-descent dips. The 21M-parameter XL model reaches state of the art and expert-level equivalence on both held-out sets. They attribute weaker large-model transfer on Helsinki to a distribution shift in late-EEG neonates.
record.recipe_differences: Supervised ConvNeXt scaling for EEG seizure classification, measured with classification metrics; not language-model pretraining or held-out cross-entropy scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with model size non-monotonically, with a double-descent dip; gains for larger models diminish on Helsinki, and the late-EEG subgroup degrades at Large and XL sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: Expert-equivalence Δκ improves with model size on Cork (-0.424 Nano to -0.094 XL) but is non-monotonic on Helsinki (Medium -0.052, Large -0.066, XL -0.082).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agreement with human experts improves monotonically with model scale in classifier settings.

record.problems: Individual values in several scaling plots are figure-only. The authors report a single-centre development dataset and a distribution shift on Helsinki, with diminished or reversed scaling behavior in the late-EEG subgroup.
record.rows_left_out: Only MCC results from the scaling sweeps are included. Other metrics plotted in Figures 2 and D2, including Pearson correlation and error rate, are omitted to keep the record focused on the principal reported scaling metric.

untested.parts: No loss-based scaling and no fitted power-law exponents. The 'power-law' description rests on a linear fit shown in a figure. The study does not test image/video generative models, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer, and scales data and model only up to 20.6M parameters and about 50k hours.
Language-model pretraining loss is not measured.
No extrapolation from small runs to larger runs.
Depth and width are scaled together; shape at fixed parameter count is not compared.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Δκ for all five model sizes on Cork and Helsinki, giving the only per-size numbers in the paper.
AUC barely moves with scale on Helsinki (Nano 0.980 vs XL 0.982) while XL has about 10x fewer false detections per hour; scaling gains depend on the metric.
Pearson r and error-rate scaling curves are omitted from the rows.

record.verdict_notes: This is a supervised classifier scaled over only about 3 orders of magnitude, measured with classification metrics rather than loss. The 'power-law' wording rests on a linear fit in Fig. 2c with no exponents reported, so its support for V5 is weak and qualitative. Most per-size values are figure-only. V7 links were removed: the departures from a clean power law here are double descent and distribution shift in a non-LM setting, not dependence of LM fits on setup or fitting choices.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss and its relation to parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations, their scaling with compute, and the relative growth rates of parameters and data.
Architecture comparisons at fixed parameter count.
The study reports supervised EEG classification metrics, not pretraining loss; it does not test image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Downstream language-model task performance or its predictability from pretraining loss.
Whether language-model fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits vary with fitting choices, and whether published language-model laws disagree.

relationships.condition: Development test split (data and model sweeps), Cork held-out set, Helsinki early-EEG subgroup
relationships.reason: MCC rises with more neonates and hours and with model size from Medium to XL. The authors call the gains approximate power laws (r1, r5–r7, r10–r12).
relationships.display_finding: MCC increased with more neonates, recording hours and model size from Medium to XL, with gains described as approximate power laws.

relationships.condition: Small model and 1k–10k-hour data range; Helsinki overall
relationships.reason: The curves are non-monotonic: a double-descent dip appears at the Small model and at mid data sizes. On Helsinki, returns diminish after Medium and the best model depends on the metric (r2, r4, r9, r14, r16, r17).
relationships.display_finding: Performance showed double-descent dips at the Small model and intermediate data sizes, while Helsinki gains diminished after Medium and depended on the metric.

relationships.condition: Helsinki late-EEG subgroup (recorded at or after 1 week)
relationships.reason: MCC peaks at Medium and degrades progressively for Large and XL. This is stated explicitly and shown in Fig. D2 (r18, r19).
relationships.display_finding: MCC peaked at Medium and progressively declined for Large and XL.
